lots.what_it_is: Ink and wash watercolour of two stylised trees above a spattered dark horizon band, boxed 'TS' monogram with 1984 lower left, catalogued by Gowans as Tony Smibert, untitled, 25.5 x 35.5 cm, red timber frame with cream mount.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The researcher supplied no entries and my own checks (Invaluable slug pages without the artist ID, Handmark search, Colville, Leonard Joel, Lawsons, Davidson, Mossgreen, MutualArt, Artsy, DAAO, Bing and DuckDuckGo) returned no Smibert prices. WebSearch budget is exhausted so the Invaluable Smibert artist ID could not be found. No currency rate used.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0.
lots.confidence_reason: Mark read (boxed TS over 1984) and the style fits Tony Smibert, but the monogram has not been checked against a reference and there is no price evidence of any kind.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 (enlarged) shows a hand-inked rectangular box containing a 'T' over an 'S'-like stroke with '1984' below, lower left under the horizon band. Not a written signature; Gowans calls it 'signed left hand side'. Calligraphic East-Asian-influenced brushwork with salt or spatter texture in the band. Photo 2 shows a cream mount with a grey line and a red timber frame.
lots.condition: Sheet looks clean in the visible area. Outer mount is soiled and discoloured at the edges. Not examined out of the frame, so foxing or toning under the mount is unknown.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there any label, gallery sticker or inscription on the back confirming Tony Smibert, and is the work on paper free of foxing or staining under the mount?

lots.what_it_is: Oil (possibly acrylic underpaint) on Morilla canvas of a white tree framed by stylised turquoise leaves under a blue sky, 50 x 39.5 cm, black frame, catalogued by Gowans as 'Tom Samek attributed'. Faint green monogram lower left on the front; 'T. Samek' handwritten on the top stretcher bar.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. Handmark Gallery (Hobart) pages opened confirm Tom Samek is represented there and that original works were being released after his death (about three years ago), but no prices are shown. Invaluable ID for Samek could not be found (WebSearch budget exhausted). No currency rate used. Note: Gowans shows a current bid of $310 after 10 bids (checked 30/09/2026), which is already above anything the evidence here can support.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. Current bid is $310 (all-in $371 at 19.8%).
lots.confidence_reason: Gowans itself says only 'attributed'; the only link to Samek is a handwritten stretcher inscription and an unclear front monogram, and there is no price evidence.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 enlarged: a small green painted mark lower left that reads as a vertical monogram (possibly 'TS'), not a written name. Photo 4 (rotated): top stretcher bar stamped 'MORILLA', a circled '6', and a handwritten 'T. Samek' in ballpoint or pencil. The stretcher and canvas look old and consistent with 1970s to 1990s Australian artist supplies. Subject is decorative and not typical of Samek's known humorous figurative work.
lots.condition: Canvas surface looks clean with no visible cracking or tears in the photos; dust on the frame lip; back of canvas lightly toned.
lots.question_for_gowans: What is the provenance behind 'originally purchased from a friend that directly knew Tom Samek', is there any documentation, and who wrote 'T. Samek' on the stretcher?

lots.working: Premium 19.8% (all-in = hammer x 1.198). Keep: the only same-item SOLD is the Aalders Trapper; price result 240 but last bid 200 and premium treatment unclear, so I use the lower 200. 200 / 1.198 = 166.9, rounded down to $165. Flip: likely resale about $200 at a regional auction (same-image sale 200-240, close comps 150-180), less 15% seller commission ($30), outbound postage $0 if consigned locally = $170. 170 / 2.396 = 70.95, rounded down to $70.
lots.confidence_reason: Plate title, date, A.P and signature all read in the photos and there is one same-image SOLD result whose page I opened, backed by several close small A/P sales; only one exact match, and the pencil signature cannot be authenticated from photos.
